Keryx, the command line

**Keryx** is Megaron's command-line client — the herald. It talks to the same server as the browser and can do everything a Wanax can do, including a few things the browser cannot do yet ([[rough-edges]]).

You do not need it to play. It exists for players who prefer a terminal, for automation, and for AI players.

## Getting started

Keryx is a single program; ask whoever runs your world for a copy. Then:

```
export POLEIA_SERVER=https://megaron.formatet.se
keryx login --username <your name>
keryx join
keryx status
```

`keryx actions` is the command to reach for when you are stuck: it lists what you can do right now. `keryx --help`, and `--help` after any command, explain the rest. The rules themselves are in this Codex: `keryx codex` lists the articles and `keryx codex <id>` prints one.

## A few useful commands

```
keryx status                 # your realm at a glance
keryx codex bronze           # read a Codex article
keryx notifications          # the archive — what happened while you were away
keryx dispatches             # which kinds of news are pushed to you live
keryx map                    # the map around you
keryx city                   # people and placement in a city
keryx goods                  # stock and production
keryx wants                  # who needs what, among cities you have contacted
keryx password               # change your password
keryx occupation order ...   # sack, burn or annex an occupied city
```

Orders given through Keryx obey the same rules as in the browser: they travel by [[runners|Runner]] and take days ([[time]]).

`POLEIA_CONFIG` selects a separate configuration file. `POLEIA_SERVER` and `POLEIA_TOKEN` override connection settings. Command failures show the error and a pointer to `keryx <command> --help`. March previews call the soldiers' silver cost **Pay**.

With exactly one active world, commands select and save it automatically. To choose explicitly, run `keryx worlds` and then `keryx worlds --select <world-id>`. City rows show both the placement number and `(q,r)`; use those coordinates with `build --hex q,r`.

Use a city name or province ID either positionally or with `--province` in `city`, `placements`, `status` and `build`. For placement: `keryx place Knossos fish 13 -1` or `keryx place --province Knossos fish 13 -1`. Put flags before the good when using a negative delta. If no citizens work that good on the chosen hex, the result lists where they do work it. `founding settle --yes` skips the question. Travel estimates use days; if an arrival cannot be calculated it is reported as unavailable.

Hex selection accepts the ordinal shown by City, with or without `#`: `build --type lumbermill --hex 6` or `--hex '#6'`. Placement can use `place fish 6 +1`, `place fish '#6' +1`, or `place --hex 6 fish +1`; `--hex q,r` also works. Put flags before the good when giving a negative delta. `staff` is for city workplaces; hex-bound buildings are worked with `place` on their hex.


## Argument reminders

Start construction with `keryx build --type harbour`. A positional argument in `build`
is the **city**, as in `keryx build Knossos --type harbour`; it is not the building type.
Use `build --list` for the catalogue or `build --queue` for queued construction.

`keryx staff olive_press` shows that named workplace's staffing. Add `+1` or `-1`
to change it; the building name is required. Use `keryx city` or `keryx roster`
to find workplaces and assignments. Hex buildings use `place`.

Send a report with `keryx report --text "what happened"`; use `--kind confused`
for a question the rules did not answer. For colony founding in scripts, add
`--yes`: `keryx unit march --unit <id> --target 5,-3 --intent colonize --name Thapsos --yes`.
Without confirmation, the non-interactive text command only shows the forecast;
JSON callers receive a refusal until they add `--yes`.

Transfers and caravans

A **transfer** moves goods between two of your *own* settlements. No consent, no negotiation — simpler than [[trade]] with a stranger.

Open **Economy → Transfer**, choose *From*, *To*, the good and the quantity, and press **Send →**. Below, **Your cargo in transit** lists everything on the road — which city it left, which city it is bound for, and the day it arrives. A notification tells you when it is delivered.

## Cargo is physical

A caravan is people and pack animals walking across the map. Others can see it on the road, but not what it carries — the cargo is a secret until someone takes it. **It can be intercepted and seized** — yours by others, theirs by you. A hostile unit on watch ([[stances|sentry]]) near the road will stop a caravan that passes. Only [[messengers]] are safe. When a land caravan is seized, both sides are told where, and exactly what cargo changed hands; the seized goods go to the raider's capital.

An internal transfer carries exactly the same risk as a trade or a gift: on land only raiders, at sea also [[sea|storms]]. Whose goods they are never changes the risk.

To move goods regularly without being there, use a [[routes|standing order]].

## Sending it by sea

When both ends are coastal or harboured and a sea lane connects them, a transfer sails instead of walking — **if you have a free Galley or Emporos waiting in the sending port** ([[sea]]). No free hull there, and no land road either, and the transfer is refused with the reason why; build one at a Shipyard, or wait for one to come home.

The ship is bound to the round trip: it cannot be given any other order until it has sailed back and unloaded, empty, at its own port. What it can carry is limited by the hull's own capacity — a heavier shipment than a Galley or Emporos can hold is refused, with the capacity and the weight both named, so you know to split it or send a bigger hull.

A laden ship caught at sea does not always lose the same way a caravan does. One of three things happens, and you are told which:

- **Captured** — the raider takes the cargo *and* the ship. It sails off under a new flag.
- **Damaged** — half the cargo is lost overboard in the fight; the ship limps home with the rest.
- **Sunk** — the cargo and the ship are both gone.

Sending to another Wanax is a [[gifts|gift or tribute]], with nothing requested in return.

## Route and journey time

Cargo follows a real route around impassable ground. Its path and the terrain costs
are fixed when each leg departs. Caravan time is **1.5 times the march time on that
same path**, rounded once to the nearest whole day, with at least one day per leg.
The return leg is priced separately because it enters different terrain. Cargo
weight limits a ship's hold; it does not change journey speed.

Without a traversable road or an eligible ship on a sea lane, a shipment is refused
before goods are taken. A standing route pauses and explains the obstacle. The
arrival day shown in your cargo list is the scheduled delivery; delays or
interception can prevent that delivery.


In Keryx, `transfer` sends from your **selected city**, which may be a colony.
Check it with `keryx status`, or choose the sending city explicitly:
`keryx transfer --from Knossos --dest Mallia --good grain --qty 50`.
The sending city cannot also be the destination. A rejected self-transfer sends
nothing; use `--from` to choose the other city you meant to send from.
